identification: Datadog ddtrace 4.2.1 Python APM, profiling and application-security source distribution
marker_line: ddtrace 4.2.1: bugfix-only diff; neutral boot task, add ACL/firewall

provenance.identity_check: Sample SHA-256 equals the PyPI 4.2.1 sdist digest returned by the registry; metadata names ddtrace and Datadog.
provenance.recovered_with: forager; original archives and .forage.json records are in scratch/version-drift/generic and github_repo.
provenance.wheels: Forager initially selected an original 4.2.0 wheel. Subsequently fetched all 52 original 4.2.0 wheels with --all-wheels; the source comparison uses the original sdist.

runtime_changes: Anthropic _on_content_block_stop_chunk now returns the message when its content list is empty, before indexing content[-1]. This prevents span construction from raising IndexError on an unmatched stop event.
ThreadInfo::unwind_tasks includes <optional> and initializes upper_python_stack_size to python_stack.size() instead of zero. The existing loop then retains asyncio frames when no _run frame is found.
decisive_diff.other_changes: Version fields in PKG-INFO (two copies) and pyproject.toml; SOURCES.txt adds an asyncio regression test; Anthropic regression test added.
decisive_diff.dependency_pin: Both releases pin system-tests to c35863e8e9f5872e27e5f6cf0be8fae82288a4ff; no dependency substitution.

execution_review: The .mdc file is editor guidance with Python/FastAPI and shell examples. The traversal string is a curl request to localhost:8000/read?filename=../../etc/passwd, labelled as a RASP blocking test. It is a real inclusion payload, so the suspicious payload finding remains accurate.

In ddtrace/appsec/_common_module_patches.py, the file-open wrapper passes filename to the WAF in the active AppSec context and raises BlockingException for block actions, otherwise forwarding the original open call. This is consistent with the documented security-testing purpose.

system-tests/utils/virtual_machine/aws_provider.py reads setup_ssh.ps1 only as Windows EC2 user_data, and creates the instance with the configured SSH key pair. ddtrace package import and setup do not run this CI provisioning script.

setup_ssh.ps1 installs OpenSSH, starts ssh-agent/sshd automatically, allows inbound TCP/22 if needed and sets the default SSH shell to PowerShell. It writes a download-key.ps1 helper and registers it as SYSTEM, highest run level, at system startup, then runs it immediately.

The helper fetches /latest/meta-data/public-keys/0/openssh-key from EC2 metadata at 169.254.169.254 into administrators_authorized_keys and applies icacls inheritance removal plus Administrators/SYSTEM grants. Despite the upstream comment saying private key, the actual URL is the assigned public key. No attacker-selected public key or remote command payload is embedded.
setup.py downloads versioned Datadog native libraries, verifies SHA-256, extracts native library members and builds extensions. It is byte-identical to the predecessor.

Decoded pygoat.xz is a tar containing an intentionally vulnerable Django application used by the explicit AppSec integration tests, including command/SQL injection checks. It is unchanged. Compression and URL encodings here do not establish malicious concealment.

relocation.unsupported_claim: Registration + SYSTEM + highest run level + startup does not establish unwanted persistence, and the trigger is OS startup rather than login.
relocation.preserved: All four required conditions, PowerShell/Windows scope, file scope and confidence. No matcher is narrowed.
relocation.intentional_widening: Removed product/CI exclusions because neutral task settings are accurate in provisioning tools too. No consumer references the old rule or its ancestor directory selectors; the new rule does not gate attack composites.
relocation.mappings: Removed inherited ATT&CK persistence/MBC mappings from this neutral settings observation.

rule_changes.new_observations: ACL grant and inheritance command text (including a generated helper); structured calls creating and querying Windows firewall rules.
rule_changes.consumer_audit: Existing ACL and firewall objective consumers reference specific existing IDs; broad filesystem consumers only add resource context. No existing objective is newly supplied an ACL-grant or firewall-operation alternative.
rule_changes.unmodified: The traversal-query payload rule and all underlying scheduled-task atoms remain unchanged.

atomscan --no-update --mode slow --format json sample (before and after, including followed artifacts)
verification.focused_controls: Nine pass: renamed real EC2 fixture, ordinary startup maintenance, four missing-condition controls, reference-only ACL/firewall near miss, existing concealed backdoor, backdoor with startup settings.
verification.retained_attack_controls: Five existing concealed-task/resource cases pass. Three distinct hostile backdoor/SSH/service composites remain in the original attack and the startup variant. The attack fixture is analyzed statically, never executed.
verification.outside_batch_benign: Gaia 0.23.0 ensure-lemonade-running.ps1 launches a CI model server as SYSTEM at boot. The old suspicious rule fired; the replacement remains notable with all task atoms retained.
verification.test_maintenance: Corrected the pre-existing socket-without-eval case to expect its current canonical process/io/stream trait, replacing a retired socket/tcp ID.
verification.fetch_scope_note: The later full scan includes additional ordinary dependency members, mainly CMake; no previously analyzed path disappears. Compare matching paths rather than raw aggregate counts.
verification.remaining_findings: Only the real traversal payload and its archive inheritance remain suspicious. The calibrated ML gate stays benign (lvl -1); raw probability changes from 0.6893272 to 0.62005776 across the full scans with different dependency expansion. No classifier miss is exposed.
verification.losses: Only the unsupported persistence label disappears from setup_ssh.ps1 and its parent archive. No retained attack detection is lost.

primary_scan.exit_reason: Accurate suspicious traversal payload remains in the AppSec example; ML gate is benign.

limits: Static review; no claim that sample code was run on a victim. Deployment authorization is not provided. An unauthorized SSH-key provisioning invocation could be abuse, but this artifact supplies explicit test-VM provisioning context. Scanner flow limitations in mixed Markdown/code and some Python files were handled by reading the source, not by assuming a clean scan proves safety.
